f sends each point radially to the unit circle. g puts that circle at radius 0.7 in the annulus.
On X, g(f(reⁱθ)) = 0.7eⁱθ. The homotopy [(1−t)·r + t·0.7]eⁱθ moves the original point to its round-trip image and stays in the annulus. On Y, f∘g is already the identity.

The top and bottom Y pictures show exactly the same intermediate output. The homotopy is in X: at t = 0 it matches the original input above, and at t = 1 it matches the composition below. The homotopy need not be one-to-one.
